review_notes: I read the whole target file and the related definitions in DefectIncrementBounds.lean (barMoment, defects, linearRows, remainders, slowSlice). The file declares no simp attributes of its own, so I looked for missing simp lemmas and awkward expansion patterns. I found one pattern: the Fin 3 vector definitions have no component lemmas, so proofs use `change` and long `simp only` lists. I did not run Lean, so I can't say how fragile that simp call actually is. The `barMoment_add_on` and `barMoment_sub_on` lemmas need membership and shell hypotheses, so they are not good simp candidates. I also did not recommend making `barMoment_apply` a simp lemma, because that would expand every moment into an integral.

findings.problem: `defects`, `linearRows` and `remainders` are defined as `![_, _, _]` vectors in `ℕ → P → Fin 3 → ℝ`. They have no component simp lemmas such as `defects_apply_zero`, `defects_apply_one` and `defects_apply_two`. As a result the proofs unfold the definitions and rely on a long, `simp?`-generated `simp only` list of `Matrix.cons_val*`, `Fin.zero_eta`, `Fin.mk_one`, `Fin.reduceFinMk` and `Matrix.head_cons` lemmas. In `linearRows_eq_neg_of_fiveRows_on` the same gap is worked around with three `change barMoment … = -(defects … i)` goals, which depend on definitional unfolding. In `remainders_mem_local` it is worked around by `fin_cases i` followed by `exact` that relies on defeq. These proofs break whenever the vector literal or the `Fin` normal form changes.
findings.proposed_change: In DefectIncrementBounds.lean, next to the definitions, add `@[simp]` component lemmas: `defects … n p 0 = pressureDefect …`, `… 1 = thetaDefect …`, `… 2 = axialDefect …`, and the analogous three each for `linearRows` and `remainders`. These are `rfl` lemmas, so they are safe and terminating. Keep `defects` itself non-simp, so the vectors are not unfolded eagerly. Then `defects_update_on` can be `funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp [hP, hT, hZ, Pi.add_apply]`, or can rewrite component by component. The `change` lines in `linearRows_eq_neg_of_fiveRows_on` become `simp only [linearRows_apply_zero, defects_apply_zero]` or plain `show` goals.
findings.benefit: Readers get one canonical way to read components of the defect, linear-row and remainder vectors. The long `Matrix.cons_val` simp lists disappear. Proofs no longer depend on how `![…]` happens to unfold.
